newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - ABF sale enables sharper focus.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - ABF sale enables sharper focus.

text.p: Associated British Foods' sale of its food retail business in Ireland will enable it to focus on its three core businesses, said finance director Martin Clark in an interview.
"ABF's principal activities are now focused on food production, agricultural products and value added food ingredients," he said.

Earlier Tesco Plc said it was buying 75 Quinnsworth and Crazy Prices stores in the Republic of Ireland and 34 stores in Northern Ireland trading as Stewarts, Crazy Prices, Superdeal, Westside Stores and Bloomfield.
"Under Don Tidey they have been developed successfully to their current significant scale and for it to go forward they would benefit from being part of a larger, focused retail group," said Clark.
With the potential growth of other British retailers in Ireland, ABF would also have found itself in competition with its customers on the food production side of its business.
The disposal was driven by a strategic motive rather than to free up funds for any imminent acquisition, said Clark.
"The sale of these businesses was not arranged because there is an investment in mind," he said.
"It was a strategic move--a serious offer and a serious buyer."
But the company, which now has a war chest of some 1.5 billion stg in net cash, is actively seeking suitable acquisitions, said Clark.
He identified the food ingredients area -- ABF owns British Sugar which is a major supplier to food manufacturers -- as holding the most potential for the group.
"We will wait for the right deals to come along, we are taking a long term view and not rushing into deals."
Tesco's offer was at such a "level it meant we were able to deal with them on an exclusive basis," said Clark, who declined to say what other offers the group had received.
"It's a price that properly values the business on its underlying earnings performance and cash flow performance," said Clark.
Tesco agreed to pay a total 630 million stg for the businesses and in addition ABF will receive a 10 million stg dividend from the businesses prior to the sale.
In the year to September 14, 1996 the businesses turned in a trading profit of about 58 million Irish pounds on turnover of 1.232 billion.
